fluff.overview:
The success of the GOL-3M Goliath prompted Corean Enterprises to take another look at four-legged 'Mech designs in the early 3050s. Seeking to avoid the problems shown by the poorly regarded Scorpion, Corean's designers on Stewart settled on an entirely new purpose for the quad chassis, creating a light reconnaissance platform rather than attempting another assault or fire support design. Introduced in 3054, the Tarantula became the first four-legged BattleMech to mount jump jets, a distinction that set it apart from all previous quad designs.

Produced at Corean Enterprises' facility on Stewart for the Free Worlds League, the Tarantula would eventually prove its worth and help spark a broader renaissance in four-legged 'Mech development during the 3060s.
fluff.capabilities:
Corean designers took advantage of the stability and maneuverability provided by a quad chassis to build an extremely agile recon 'Mech. Built on a Corean IX Standard chassis with a massive Nissan 200 XL engine, the Tarantula achieves a top speed approaching 130 km/h. Eight Rawlings 75 jump jets propel the 'Mech up to 240 meters, allowing it to navigate rough terrain with ease. The resulting design combines the squat, four-legged look of the Scorpion with the sleek lines of the Mercury, offering a noticeably comfortable ride with improved stability and handling that serve as key factors in winning pilots over to the unusual design.

The Tarantula's weapons complement is light but well suited to its role. A pair of Magna Mk II medium lasers mounted in pods on the upper surface provide most of its striking power, backed by a Hovertec Streak SRM-2 in the center torso for exploiting weak spots in enemy armor. Protected by four and a half tons of StarSlab/2 armor, the Tarantula carries roughly three-quarters of its theoretical maximum protection. While this leaves the design vulnerable to concentrated fire, its extraordinary speed makes it capable of avoiding most damage, and once a pilot grows accustomed to the different feel of a four-legged 'Mech, the Tarantula proves clearly superior to bipedal 'Mechs of similar specifications.
fluff.history:
The Tarantula's early service was marked by deep resistance from the MechWarrior community. Quadrupedal designs carried a strong stigma among pilots, and the Tarantula initially had to be assigned on a voluntary basis. Corean Enterprises launched a comprehensive marketing campaign that included promotional holovids, battle footage with MechWarrior testimonials, and even donated machines to appropriate units. Despite these efforts, the Tarantula was far ahead of its time, and only the broader quad renaissance of the 3060s, which produced designs like the Sirocco and the Barghest, enabled it to find wider acceptance.

The turning point for the Tarantula came through an unlikely source. The wild exploits of the Seventeenth Recon Regiment in the Draconis Combine drew attention to the new ZPH-4A variant, pushing it to an unexpectedly large market: the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery. The DCMS High Command grudgingly accepted the Tarantula's potency and assigned machines to well-known units such as the Legion of Vega and the Proserpina Hussars. Corean Enterprises was happy to exploit the irony that an undisciplined mercenary group had created demand for the design within House Kurita's generally anti-mercenary military culture.

The Tarantula's production history reflects the turbulent politics of Stewart itself. The Corean Enterprises MacAdams-Suharno facility remained under Free Worlds League control through the Clan Invasion and Civil War eras, producing successive variants as demand grew. During the Jihad, the Word of Blake seized control of Stewart and its factories. Following the liberation, the Republic of the Sphere administered the world before it eventually declared independence during the Dark Age. By the ilClan era, Clan Wolf had claimed Stewart, though Tarantula production had largely ceased by then.

Perhaps the Tarantula's most significant legacy was unintentional. When Clan Cloud Cobra scientists acquired the remains of an Inner Sphere Tarantula, they used it as the basis for their own quad design, the Stalking Spider. This Clan reinterpretation of the Tarantula concept proved that the fundamental design philosophy behind Corean's four-legged scout was sound, even if it took a Clan engineering team to fully exploit its potential.
fluff.deployment: A Dark Age era field refit based on the ZPH-4A, this variant replaces the extended-range PPC with an extended-range large laser and upgrades the C3 slave unit to a C3 boosted slave for improved networking range. The MASC system and armor protection of the 4A are retained, maintaining the fast sniper role while adapting to the networking requirements of Republic and post-Republic era combined-arms formations. As a field modification rather than a factory variant, the 5A has appeared across multiple successor states wherever Tarantulas and the necessary components are available.
